3: The Town of Pine Mountain, Georgia (the “Town”) desires to adopt an ordinance governing the registration, use and operation of personal transportation vehicles on the authorized streets and personal transportation vehicle paths located within the Town pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 40-6-331 and other applicable law.

“Authorized streets” means all such streets, roads and public rights-of-way located within the Town that are not owned and maintained by Harris County, Georgia or the State of Georgia. The Town Clerk shall maintain a list of authorized streets, and such list may be amended from time to time by the Town Council. The term “authorized” streets shall also include designated crossings at (1) the intersection of U.S. Highway 27 and Chipley Street and (2) the intersection of King Avenue and State Road 18/West Harris Street.

As described in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(39), “operator” means any person who drives or is in actual physical control of a motor vehicle or who causes a fully autonomous vehicle to move or travel with the automated driving system engaged.

As described in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(43.4), “personal transportation vehicle” or “PTV” means any motor vehicle: (1) with a minimum of four wheels; (2) capable of maximum level ground speed of less than twenty (20) miles per hour; (3) with a maximum gross vehicle unladed or empty weight of 1,375 pounds; and (4) capable of transporting not more than eight (8) persons. PTV shall be deemed to be inclusive of golf carts, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(17.3) that otherwise meet the requirements for a PTV. For purposes hereof, PTV shall also include any motor vehicle that meets all requirements for a lowspeed vehicle, but for the fact that said motor vehicle does not have a Vehicle Identification Number. Notwithstanding the foregoing, all-terrain vehicles, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 40- 1-1(3), and multipurpose off-highway vehicles, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1(33.1), are not deemed PTVs for purposes of this Ordinance. PTVs are the only motor vehicles authorized under this section.

As described in O.C.G.A. § 40-1-1-(43.5), “personal transportation vehicle path” or “PTV path” means a right of way under the jurisdiction and control of this state or a local political subdivision thereof designated for use by personal transportation vehicle drivers.

General. It shall be the duty of every owner of a PTV that is operated over the authorized streets, PTV paths, and those areas accessible by the public to register the PTV and have said PTV inspected as required by the Town before any PTV shall proceed on the streets.

Permit Required. No person shall operate a PTV: a. which is not permitted through the Town as provided herein on an annual basis. The permit is to be placed on the front cover driver side; and b. without a valid driver’s license. Application. Every application for a permit shall be made on a form supplied by the Town and shall contain the following information: Name, address and phone number of applicant; . Make, model, name and PTV ID number; . Current driver’s license number; . Certification that the PTV is roadworthy; and . Proof of liability insurance (if required under applicable law). Other such information that the Town may require. Revocation of Permit. Permits will be revoked if it is found that the permit holder: a. no longer has a valid driver’s license; b. has failed to abide by the rules and regulations of this Ordinance or applicable state law; c. has failed to abide by traffic laws in the use of a PTV on authorized streets or PTV paths; d. has failed to grant right-of-way to pedestrians and bicyclists as required by law; e. has allowed an ineligible person to operate the PTV in violation of this Ordinance; f. cannot safely operate the PTV on the roadway or poses a threat to the safety of others as determined in reasonable discretion of the Town or its Chief of Police; g. has failed to maintain the vehicle in roadworthy condition; or 1. has failed to pay the registration fee required hereunder. Resident Fee. The registration fee for PTVs shall be $15.00 for residents residing inside the Town limits as determined by the applicant’s driver’s license. Registration shall be effective for one (1) year unless the PTV is transferred to a new owner or registration is revoked by the Town. Registration fees shall be paid to the Town Clerk. The resident fee will not be prorated for the first year of registration. Bills are mailed annually to the owner of record. Non-resident Fee. The registration fee for the PTVs shall be $15.00. Those who live outside the Pine Mountain Town limits and do not pay Pine Mountain property taxes must also pay a $150.00 non-resident per year user fee. Upon transfer of ownership a PTV to another person who shall operate the PTV over the authorized streets or PTV paths of the Town, the new owner of said PTV shall provide to the Town a notice of such change in ownership, in addition to such other information as the Town may require in its reasonable discretion, and a transfer fee of $15.00 within ten (10) days of such change in ownership. If the permit is not transferred within ten (10) business days, a $25.00 penalty will be applied in addition to the $15.00 registration charge, and the PTV shall be considered an unregistered cart after the ten-business day period.

- (7) Prohibitions. A golf course, resort, or other business venture that utilizes PTVs in the ordinary course of business shall not be granted a permit hereunder for said PTVs.

Gasoline Carts

- (1) | Every PTV powered by gasoline shall at all times be equipped with an exhaust system in good working order and meet the following specifications:

- a) The exhaust system shall include the piping leading from the flange of the exhaust manifold to and including the muffler and exhaust pipes and any other related parts all as specified by the manufacturer.

- b) The exhaust system and its elements shall be securely fastened, with brackets or hangers which are designed for the particular purpose of fastening a PTV exhaust system.

- c) The engine and powered mechanism of every PTV shall be so equipped, adjusted and tuned so that the exhaust equals the same amount of a PTV in good working order.

- (2) It shall be unlawful for the owner of any PTV to operate or permit the operation of such PTV, when any device installed by the manufacturer for the purpose of controlling or abating atmospheric emissions, has been removed or rendered unserviceable by removal, alteration or other action that would interfere with its otherwise proper operation.

The operator shall possess a valid motor vehicle driver’s license and be at least sixteen (16) years of age, except as described in Subsection (b) below.

Any person who possesses a valid learner’s permit and is at least fifteen (15) years of age may operate a PTV in accordance with this Ordinance, so long as such person is accompanied in the front seat by a person who possesses a valid motor vehicle class C driver’s license and is at least eighteen (18) years of age.

All operators of PTVs shall abide by all traffic regulations applicable to vehicular traffic when using the Town streets and those areas legally accessible by the public (except sidewalks, ball fields and walking trails), including without limitation, the Uniform Rules of the Road as set forth in O.C.G.A. §40-6-1, et seq.

No PTV is to be driven on any street where the speed limit is greater than 25 mph or any other street that the Mayor and Council or Police Chief, in their sole discretion, deem to be unsafe for use.

All PTVs permitted hereunder shall be equipped as outlined in O.C.G.A. § 40-8-35, and are equipped with all required lighting to operate during low or no light conditions.

No PTV shall be permitted to operate over, along or across state highways except at designated PTV crossing areas. No PTV may park in designated parking spaces or otherwise on state highways.

No individual or group shall engage in hazardous activities on the streets and those areas accessible by the public. Such hazardous activities, and the special rules pertaining to them, include, but are not limited to, the following:

- (1) Racing in any form

- (2) Blocking of public access, except for special events approved by the Town

- (3) Normal rules of the road shall apply

- (4) Pedestrians should be given due consideration and reasonable right-of-way

- (5) All laws and local ordinances relative to alcohol and its use, including open container laws, which apply to traffic on the streets of the Town of Pine Mountain, also apply to PTVs. All litter shall be retained by the PTV operator for proper disposal later. Littering on the streets of the Town shall be subject to the fines and penalties as prescribed under applicable law.

- (6) Any other act or omission that would be a violation of the laws and local ordinances which apply to traffic enforcement codes on the streets of the Town of Pine Mountain.

Each person using the streets of the Town of Pine Mountain is liable for their own actions. Liability insurance coverage varies and each person operating a PTV on the public streets, PTV paths, and those areas legally accessible by the public should verify their coverage. Nothing in this section shall be construed as an assumption of liability by the Town for any injuries to persons or property which may result from the operation of a PTV by a permit holder or the failure by the Town of Pine Mountain to revoke said permit.
7: The operation of personal transportation vehicles under the following circumstances shall not be subject to the provisions of this Ordinance: (1) The operation of personal transportation vehicles at golf courses, private clubs, or on private property, with the consent of the landowner; (2) The operation of golf carts on private streets within gated or limited access communities; (3) The operation of golf carts in connection with a parade, festival, or other special event authorized by the Town, provided that the consent of the event sponsor is obtained and provided that such use only occurs during the special event; (4) The use of PTVs by the Town law enforcement on official law enforcement business or by other Town personnel for official business on Town-controlled property, including cemeteries, parks, green space, and other property as needed; provided however, that such PTVs shall comply with the technical and operating requirements of this Ordinance .

Such improvements shall be made prior to the effective date of this Ordinance.

Any person who violates the terms of this Ordinance shall be subject to such fines, penalties, and punishments provided in the Town’s ordinances or applicable state law. The Town reserves the right to take possession of and impound a PTV that is used in violation of this Ordinance. Any violation of this Ordinance shall be charged against the registered owner of the PTV, and all fines and penalties shall be levied against the registered owner of the PTV as follows: (1) For the first offense, a fine of not less than $50.00 (2) For the second offense, a fine of not less than $100.00 (3) Ifa third offense is committed within one year of conviction for a second offense, the minimum fines shall be $250.00 and the registered owner’s PTV registration shall be revoked. The registered owner or family member cannot thereafter register a cart for use in the Town for a period of two years following conviction of a third offense.
